# Compact Language Detector 2

From [CLD2Owners/cld2](https://github.com/CLD2Owners/cld2), revision
`b56fa78a2fe44ac2851bae5bf4f4693a0644da7b`, under the Apache 2.0 license
in `LICENSE`. The only source modification is recorded in
`cxx11-byte-table.patch`: a diagnostic pragma around one generated byte table
lets modern GCC/Clang accept its negative initializers. These encode signed
relative offsets as modulo-256 unsigned bytes. The table bytes are unchanged.

`sources.list` selects the default, approximately 83-language Chrome tables
from upstream's `internal/compile_libs.sh`. Only those sources and their
transitive quoted includes are vendored. The larger full-language tables,
tools and test data are omitted. `upstream-sha256.json` records the original
bytes, including the license, for verifying an update before applying the
patch. CMake and Make both read the same source list. The literal list in
`tools/build-modern-browser.py` must also be kept in sync: release CI parses
that list without running Python. `docs/cld2-license.txt` carries the same
license in CI's documentation-based package layout.

Summit's wrapper validates UTF-8 with CLD2's checked API and bounds the input.
Detection is local and uses the page's text; a declared HTML language does not
override the result. Short, mixed or uncertain samples do not trigger an
automatic translation offer.
